labels.uncertainty: The letter is clearly ח. The mark after it looks like two small strokes, so it is probably gershayim (״). Because it sits right at the start of the line, I can't rule out a single geresh (׳).

The second letter has a separate left leg, so I read it as ה rather than ר, but the type is very small. I read the gershayim as two strokes. The label runs straight into קדוש with almost no space, and the period after the preceding ואמר is separate from the label.
Clearly ח with gershayim. The colon before it belongs to the end of the preceding כבודו, not to the label.
ה versus ר is the same small-type issue as the קדוש label, but I lean ה. The mark is gershayim. The period before the label belongs to the end of יאמרו.
ח with gershayim. The colon before it closes ממקומו.

ה versus ר is uncertain as above, but I lean ה. A small dot sits between the gershayim and the י of ימלך. It could be a stray point, a raised period, or part of the vowel marking on י. I don't count it as part of the abbreviation.
ח with gershayim. The colon before it closes הללויה.

notes: I read the labels only from the shapes of the letters, not from who usually recites each verse. The four alternating labels (ח״ / קה״) all look consistent with each other.
The main uncertainty everywhere is ה versus ר as the second letter of the קה״ labels, because the type is so small. Wherever the image was clearest, I saw a separate left leg, which points to ה.
None of the labels has a period after it. The punctuation next to them belongs to the main text.
